rules.searched: Done when all four discovery processes (stock, updated literature, grey, tool) are marked searched in the progress ledger for this table, at table level or for any sub-practice; not started when there is no ledger activity and no logged search.
rules.acquired: Done when every source the acquisition queue lists for this table is in hand (none pending); not started when the queue lists no sources for it.
rules.extracted: Done when evidence units exist and no acquired source is waiting to be read; not started when there are no active evidence units.
rules.reviewed: Done when at least 50% of evidence units have a human review decision (signed off, or rejected and dropped); not started when none have.
rules.synthesised: Done when the generated table has rows, matches its synthesis report, and the report lists no unmapped variables (decision-parked families are shown but do not block); not started when the table has no rows.
rules.prose: Done when every row has written prose; not started when none do.
rules.benchmarked: Done when both the seed benchmark table and the benchmark write-up exist; in progress when only one does.

meta.completion_rule: Completion = round(100 × (stages done + 0.5 × stages in progress) / 7). It measures pipeline position, not evidence quality.

decisions.question: The re-prose pass over the 30 conflicting rows found six where the sides answer DIFFERENT questions, so the conflict is an artefact of pooling (the same pattern as the water-stress split): (1) WH production_gap highland and cross_family - losses are fanya juu / soil bunds at 1030-1454 mm rainfall, gains are tied ridges / mulching / stone bunds at 695-1139 mm, so sub-practice and rainfall co-vary; (2) WH in_situ water_quality - a nutrient loss from minimum tillage vs sediment ratings for pits and bunds; (3) FR cross_family water_stress - infiltration up in 83 pct of studies vs groundwater recharge down in 67 pct, different outcomes from one review; (4) FR active_planting biodiversity - losses vs natural regeneration, gains on bare dunes with no control, so the separator is siting; (5) AF linear_boundary drought - live-fence fodder vs crop losses beside shelterbelts; (6) wetland heat - one study's day vs night cycle.
decisions.options: A split where the separator is a variable or sub-practice we already have | B leave as conflicts with the separator stated in prose (current) | C case by case
decisions.recommendation: B is already live (every separator is stated in the row's conditionality); A needs new XW routes or targets per case, so C - say which of the six are worth a split and they get the water-stress treatment | Pete 2026-10-19 answered all six: (1) envelope-misfit — withhold author-attributed waterlogging losses from the production class, log as performance caveat + deferred T4 pointer; (2) min till alone is not in-situ water harvesting — 17 units wrong_practice; (3) downstream users decide — soil_permeability route removed, recharge re-routed to catchment_water_yield; (4) plantations are a separate category (tree farming, NbS alignment to check) — family split scoped, roll-up question open; (5) leave as conflict, narrative per aggregation strongly linked to evidence chain; (6) wetland heat has no rural receptor — routes off via xw_route_policy.
decisions.decided: all six answered; splits/rules per item

decisions.question: What happens when evidence is mixed: positive and negative votes balancing must not read as a neutral average, while null votes agreeing on no effect legitimately do.
decisions.options: near-tie signed class (old) | conflicting_evidence outcome (IPCC) | leave
decisions.recommendation: Pete 2026-10-19: 'we need more of an IPCC table approach - there is a difference if we have positive and negative votes making a neutral average vs neutral votes making a neutral average.' Implemented: when the minority sign carries >= 1/3 of the SIGNED weight the cell states conflicting_evidence; no_relationship stays reserved for genuine nulls. Threshold is a named constant, flagged for tuning.

decisions.question: Mangroves sat as a family under forest_restoration; the World Bank team wants them pilotable as their own restoration category.
decisions.options: family under forest_restoration (old) | own NbS (new)
decisions.recommendation: Pete 2026-10-19: 'on mangroves these will be a separate category of restoration in the project and the worldbank team want to include these for pilot.' 149 units / 26 sources re-homed; one family (tidal_coastal) pending MFL scheme sign-off; three mangrove WB evaluations unlocked for extraction.
decisions.decided: mangrove_restoration is its own NbS, pilot-bound

decisions.question: The comparator policy routes existing-wetland evidence into the restoration_rewetting family row, where it VOTES. That row now reads moderate_positive on income households already draw from existing wetlands (Rwanda cultivation, Uganda product sales, Lao fish catches) while the measured restoration studies in the same row (both Poyang, GCF Uganda) are negative or null.
decisions.options: A existing-wetland units become a non-voting note in their home family too (like reference_*) | B keep them voting in the home family (as ratified) | C a separate 'existing wetland use' row
decisions.recommendation: A for livelihood/poverty cells at least - existing-use income is the OPPORTUNITY COST of rewetting, and letting it vote as a benefit inverts the sign of the family row | Pete 2026-10-16: existing-use income is the opportunity cost of restoring; it is now a non-voting note in rural_poverty and production_gap cells everywhere, home family included.

decisions.question: forest_restoration water_stress reads 'strongly reduces water stress' on 0.53 agreement: the positive side is mostly practitioner ratings plus one modelled projection, the negative side is two meta-analyses finding catchment yield and baseflow DOWN in most cases, worst at the driest sites.
decisions.options: A split the cell (infiltration / dry-season supply vs catchment yield) | B re-derive the class with design weight dominant | C leave
decisions.recommendation: A - one cell is doing two jobs and the answers point opposite ways | Pete 2026-10-16: 'how does forest restoration help with drought stress for rural farmers? it is spatially distanced. The catchment results for downstream use are valid. Sure split the cells A.' Implemented: new T5 priority catchment_water_yield; water_yield re-routed to it; water_stress keeps local infiltration / dry-season supply.

decisions.question: Rewetting lowers CO2 and raises methane; with no gas variable both halves of one sentence enter a pool as opposite signs, so agreeing sources read as disagreement and one carbon row is wrong-signed.
decisions.options: A1 gas tag on the unit | A2 per-gas variables | A3 leave
decisions.recommendation: A1 - cheapest, no schema reshape | Pete 2026-10-16: 'for wetland restoration we need to know the CO2e net change - does methane emission exceed carbon removal? not point just having part of the picture it could be misleading.' So a single-gas unit may NOT set a carbon class; the class comes from net CO2e. Where a cell has no net figure, it reports that instead of a class.
decisions.decided: A — net CO2e decides the class

decisions.question: The wetland poverty row reads positive on society-level benefit-cost and existing-wetland income, while the only matched household study is negative; scope rows contradict the roll-up.
decisions.options: C1 household-beneficiary units only set a poverty class | C2 weight society down | C3 leave
decisions.recommendation: C1 - society value reported alongside, never summed into a household class | Pete 2026-10-16: 'C1, keep society level evidence separate.' A poverty class is set only by units whose benefit accrues to the household; society-level value is reported beside it, never summed into it.

decisions.question: Restored-vs-INTACT-reference shortfalls currently vote as harm, outvoting gains measured against the degraded baseline; two rows read as 'restoration decreases' when no unit says so.
decisions.options: B1 new comparator reference_wetland, out of the sign vote | B2 keep in vote | B3 drop the units
decisions.recommendation: B1 - mirrors the ratified existing_forest handling; fixes both rows | Pete 2026-10-16: 'this is not a useful comparison, a more sensible baseline is needed (e.g. compared to what was there before the wetland was created or restored or how the wetland increases biodiversity in the landscape, catchment or meta-population/ecological network, how it could increase landscape connectivity).' Restored-vs-intact-reference units are kept as a recovery note and never vote on the class; the counterfactual baseline is the pre-restoration state.

decisions.question: Should a T3/T6 row be published when its whole pool is one second-hand sentence or an expert assertion? Four wetland rows and one riparian row are in that state today.
decisions.options: A publish all (as now) | B evidence floor, empty cell says what is missing | C publish with an asserted-only marker
decisions.recommendation: B (floor: two independent sources, or one measured finding - Pete to pick which) | Pete 2026-10-16: "thin rows = B - 'data deficient' option". Floor: two independent sources OR one measured finding; below it the row publishes with its evidence, no class, and a reason naming what is missing.

decisions.question: Riparian has no row in comparator_policy.csv, so the seven units tagged as EXISTING-forest retention (mature spruce left beside a clear-cut, not buffer establishment) currently set the roll-up. Forest restoration keeps that evidence out; riparian does not.
decisions.options: A add a riparian row keeping existing-forest out of the roll-up (as forest restoration) | B accept it into the roll-up | C demote it
decisions.recommendation: A - the same reasoning you ratified for forest restoration applies unchanged | Pete 2026-10-16: retained mature forest beside a clear-cut is evidence for keeping riparian vegetation, not establishing a buffer. Policy row added; out of the roll-up and of every family but the unit's own.

decisions.options: A allow crop scope for wetland peatland | B leave as is | C allow for all wetland families
